messages.text: Write a job ad for a barista.

**Barista Wanted!**
We're looking for a passionate, friendly barista to join our team!
Responsibilities: prepare espresso drinks, provide excellent customer service, keep the work area clean.
Requirements: previous experience preferred, strong communication skills, ability to work in a fast-paced environment.
Apply today!

slides.note: No hours, no pay, no reason to pick this café.

cards.title: Job ad brief
cards.text: Write a job ad for [ROLE] at [BUSINESS] in [AREA]. Hours: [DAYS + TIMES]. Pay: [RATE]. Must have: [2–3 MUST-HAVES]. Nice to have: [ANY]. Why work here: [2–3 REAL REASONS]. How to apply: [STEPS]. Tone: friendly and plain, like we talk. Under 120 words. Don't use 'fast-paced' or 'rockstar'.

caption:
How to write a job ad with AI: one-line prompt vs a proper brief

Prompt A was "Write a job ad for a barista." It came back with "passionate", "fast-paced" and no hours or pay.

Prompt B was a short brief. Copy this:

"Write a job ad for [ROLE] at [BUSINESS] in [AREA]. Hours: [DAYS + TIMES]. Pay: [RATE]. Must have: [2–3 MUST-HAVES]. Nice to have: [ANY]. Why work here: [2–3 REAL REASONS]. How to apply: [STEPS]. Tone: friendly and plain, like we talk. Under 120 words. Don't use 'fast-paced' or 'rockstar'."

On an invented café, B put the hours and pay in the second line, kept the real perks and ended with a clear next step: 3 lines about you, then a short paid trial shift.

The AI can only be specific if you are. Two minutes on the brief does the work.
